name: Nahnu Video For Bunny Stream (Bunny.net)
author: Jaime Alnassim

sections.description:
Disclaimer: this is an independent, third-party plugin. It is not made by, affiliated with, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected to Bunny.net. “Bunny Stream” and “Bunny.net” are the trademarks of their own owner, referenced here only to describe what this plugin connects to.

Nahnu Video connects your WordPress site to your Bunny Stream video library, so you can drop videos into posts and pages with a shortcode or a block: a plain, real Bunny player, exactly like pasting Bunny’s own embed code, without hand-coding an iframe every time.

100% free. No premium version, no upsells, no feature paywall. Every feature described here, sync, shortcodes, blocks, the Video Control screen, the Shortcode Generator, statistics, is included, full stop. The only thing you pay for is your own Bunny Stream account, since that’s where your videos are actually hosted.

What it does

  • Syncs your Bunny Stream library into WordPress, either manually or on a schedule.
  • Organizes videos with real WordPress categories and tags, so you get related-video filtering and grid shortcodes for free.
  • [bunny_video] shortcode: a single video, Bunny’s own player with optional label/note overlays.
  • [bunny_grid] shortcode: a 1 to 6 column responsive grid, filterable by category or tag.
  • [bunny_playlist] shortcode: one live main player with a click-to-switch thumbnail grid below it, like a YouTube playlist.
  • A “Nahnu Video”, “Nahnu Video Grid”, and “Nahnu Video Playlist” block for the block editor, with a searchable video picker and live preview, no shortcode syntax to remember.
  • A Video Control admin screen: thumbnails, live search, one-click shortcode copy, and category/tag editing.
  • A dedicated Shortcode Generator page: pick a video (or videos, for a grid or playlist), set every option, live preview, copy.
  • Autoplay, loop, muted, and preload are real site-wide settings, overridable per embed. Bunny’s own player handles everything else natively.
  • An optional Bunny webhook, so new uploads, finished encodes and changes show up within seconds instead of at the next sync.
  • A developer integration API: other plugins that upload videos to Bunny Stream (an offload plugin, an upload form, a course builder) can import, refresh, or remove one video by its GUID right away. See “For Developers” below.

How to use it

Once your library is synced (see Installation below), you can drop a video in anywhere you’d normally write a shortcode or use a block:

A single video, using the ID shown in Nahnu Video → All Videos:

[bunny_video id="128"]

The same video with a corner label and a note:

[bunny_video id="128" label="NEW" note="Updated for 2026"]

A responsive grid of everything tagged “tutorials”, 3 columns wide:

[bunny_grid tag="tutorials" columns="3"]

A playlist: one main player, with a click-to-switch grid of every video in the “webinars” category below it:

[bunny_playlist category="webinars"]

Prefer the block editor? Type /nahnu or /bunny while writing a post to find “Nahnu Video”, “Nahnu Video Grid”, and “Nahnu Video Playlist”, each with a searchable picker and a live preview, no attributes to remember. Don’t want to hand-type shortcode attributes either way? Nahnu Video → Shortcode Generator builds the exact shortcode for you with a live preview and a one-click copy button.

Requirements

You’ll need your own Bunny Stream account with a video library already set up. Nahnu Video does not host or transcode video itself. It’s a WordPress-side companion to your existing Bunny library.

This plugin is not made by, affiliated with, or endorsed by Bunny.net. “Bunny Stream” is a product of Bunny.net; Nahnu Video is an independent, third-party integration.

External services

This plugin connects your WordPress site to Bunny.net‘s Stream product, a paid, third-party video hosting and delivery service. Bunny.net is required for this plugin to function; you’ll need your own Bunny Stream account and video library.

What is sent, and when

  • When you enter your Library ID, Stream API Key, and Pull Zone under Nahnu Video → Settings and click Test Connection, those credentials are sent to Bunny’s API (video.bunnycdn.com) to confirm they’re valid.
  • When you click Sync Now (or an automatic sync runs, if enabled), your Library ID and API Key are sent to Bunny’s API to retrieve your video list (titles, durations, thumbnails, view counts, and Bunny’s internal video IDs), which is then stored in your WordPress database.
  • If you enable watch-time Statistics, refreshing stats sends your Library ID, API Key, and a specific video’s ID to Bunny’s statistics API to retrieve view/watch-time data.
  • When another plugin on your site uses this plugin’s integration API to import or refresh a specific video (for example right after it uploads that video to Bunny), your Library ID, API Key, and that video’s ID are sent to Bunny’s API to fetch that one video’s details. While the video is still encoding, the same request is repeated a few times over the following hour until it’s ready.
  • If you add this plugin’s webhook URL in your Bunny dashboard, Bunny sends a small notification to your site (the library ID, the video’s ID, and a status number) whenever a video changes. Your site then fetches that video’s details from Bunny’s API as above. Nothing is sent to Bunny by setting this up; you add the URL in Bunny yourself, and can remove it there at any time.
  • None of the above happens unless you’ve entered credentials and explicitly triggered the action (or turned on auto-sync, set up the webhook, or installed a plugin that uses the integration API yourself). This plugin never sends your site’s content, user data, or visitor data to Bunny.

What visitors’ browsers connect to directly

When a site visitor views a page containing an embedded video (via [bunny_video], [bunny_grid], [bunny_playlist], or the block editor equivalents), their own browser loads the video player and thumbnails directly from Bunny’s servers (player.mediadelivery.net and your *.b-cdn.net Pull Zone), the same as it would for any embedded video from any provider. This means the visitor’s IP address and standard browser request data reach Bunny directly, not through this plugin or your server.

Bunny.net’s own terms and privacy policy govern how they handle this data:

  • Bunny.net Terms of Service
  • Bunny.net Privacy & Data Policy

For Developers

Everything below is also documented, with copyable examples, under Nahnu Video → Usage in your dashboard.

Integration API, for plugins that put videos into Bunny Stream

If your plugin uploads videos to Bunny Stream itself (an offload plugin, an upload form, a course builder), tell Nahnu Video about each one by its Bunny GUID and it shows up right away instead of at the next sync. Every call fetches the video’s real data from Bunny with Nahnu Video’s own API key, so your plugin only says which video to look at. Nahnu Video never deletes or changes anything in Bunny.

Check it’s available (and pointed at the same library) first:

if ( function_exists( 'nahnu_video_api_version' ) && version_compare( nahnu_video_api_version(), '1.0', '>=' ) && nahnu_video_library_id() === $my_library_id ) { ... }

Right after uploading a video to Bunny:

$post_id = nahnu_video_import( $guid, array( 'library_id' => $library_id, 'source' => 'my-plugin', 'attachment_id' => $attachment_id ) );

Returns the Nahnu Video post ID or a WP_Error. All arguments after $guid are optional; source and attachment_id are saved on the post so both plugins can link to each other. While Bunny is still encoding, Nahnu Video checks back automatically (after 1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 30 and 60 minutes) until the thumbnail and duration are final.

Functions:

  • nahnu_video_import( $guid, $args ): import or update one video now. Returns post ID or WP_Error.
  • nahnu_video_refresh( $guid, $args ): re-pull one already-imported video. Pass 'import_if_missing' => true to import it if it isn’t there yet.
  • nahnu_video_remove( $guid, $args ): move a video’s post to the Trash after you deleted it from Bunny.
  • nahnu_video_get_post_id( $guid ): post ID for a GUID, 0 if not imported. Imports nothing.
  • nahnu_video_get_guid( $post_id ): the GUID stored on a post.
  • nahnu_video_get_post_id_by_attachment( $attachment_id ): the post imported with that attachment_id.
  • nahnu_video_library_id(): the Bunny Library ID Nahnu Video is connected to.
  • nahnu_video_api_version(): the integration API version (currently 1.0), separate from the plugin version.
  • nahnu_video_webhook_url(): the Bunny webhook URL. It contains a secret key, so only show it to administrators.
  • nahnu_video_render( $guid_or_post_id, $args ): the same HTML as [bunny_video]. Also accepts the full attribute array, as before.

Fire-and-forget actions (they do nothing if Nahnu Video isn’t active, so your plugin doesn’t need to depend on it):

  • do_action( 'nahnu_video_import_guid', $guid, $args )
  • do_action( 'nahnu_video_refresh_guid', $guid, $args )
  • do_action( 'nahnu_video_remove_guid', $guid, $args )

When you pass library_id in $args, any GUID from a different library is refused instead of silently failing later.

Actions Nahnu Video fires

  • nahnu_video_loaded( $api_version ): everything is loaded and ready.
  • nahnu_video_synced( $post_id, $bunny_video, $is_new, $args ): one video was created/updated by a sync, import or refresh. $args['context'] says which.
  • nahnu_video_sync_completed( $result ): a full sync finished (created, updated, skipped, removed, total, manual).
  • nahnu_video_removed( $post_id, $guid, $context ): a post was moved to the Trash because its video is gone from Bunny.
  • nahnu_video_deleted( $guid, $post_id, $attachment_id ): a post is about to be permanently deleted. Nahnu Video never deletes the video in Bunny; that choice is yours.
  • nahnu_video_webhook_received( $guid, $status, $payload ): an authenticated Bunny webhook arrived for this library.
  • Also: nahnu_video_stats_refreshed, nahnu_video_term_added, nahnu_video_term_removed, nahnu_video_before_render.

Filters

  • nahnu_video_bunny_credentials( $credentials ): supply the Library ID and API key from another plugin so they aren’t entered twice. Only fill in empty values, so what’s typed into Settings still wins.
  • nahnu_video_should_import( $should, $bunny_video, $existing_id, $args ): return false to skip a video.
  • nahnu_video_insert_post_args( $post_args, $bunny_video, $is_new, $args ): change the post data before it’s saved, e.g. use the Media Library attachment’s title instead of Bunny’s file name.
  • nahnu_video_remove_missing_on_sync( $enabled ): return false to keep videos that no longer exist in Bunny.
  • nahnu_video_refresh_retry_delays( $delays, $guid ): seconds between “still encoding?” checks. An empty array turns them off.
  • nahnu_video_webhook_imports_new( $import, $guid ): return false so the webhook only refreshes existing videos.
  • nahnu_video_html( $html, $video, $atts ): change the final embed HTML for a video.
  • Also: nahnu_video_render_args, nahnu_video_grid_render_args, nahnu_video_grid_html, nahnu_video_embed_params, nahnu_video_cdn_urls, nahnu_video_query_args, nahnu_video_stats, nahnu_video_can_edit_terms, nahnu_video_default_settings.

REST endpoints

  • GET /wp-json/nahnu-video/v1/stats/{id} and GET /wp-json/nahnu-video/v1/stats: public, read-only play count and watch time.
  • POST /wp-json/nahnu-video/v1/bunny-webhook?key=...: receives Bunny Stream webhooks. Requires the secret key from Settings. The payload is only used to learn which video changed; that video’s data is always re-fetched from Bunny.

Other functions

nahnu_video_render_grid(), `nahnu_video_get_video_data()`, `nahnu_video_query()`, `nahnu_video_get_related()`, `nahnu_video_get_stats()`, `nahnu_video_get_top_videos()`, `nahnu_video_refresh_stats()`.<h3>Known Limitations</h3>

* If Hover Preview is turned on, thumbnails may not load in the block editor’s live preview for the Nahnu Video / Nahnu Video Grid blocks.
* The Nahnu Video Playlist block’s thumbnail grid may not load thumbnails in the block editor’s live preview.

Both of these are editor-preview issues only, what visitors actually see on the published page is unaffected. This is a free plugin maintained in our spare time, and this particular editor-preview quirk needs more time to track down properly than we’ve been able to give it so far. It’s also our first time building real block editor integration ourselves, we normally just build with shortcodes, so there’s a real learning curve on our end with how the block editor’s preview machinery works internally. We’re not too worried about it precisely because the front end works correctly; we’ll keep chipping away at the editor preview itself in a future update.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the nahnu-video-for-bunny-stream-bunny-net folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it through the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Nahnu Video → Settings and enter your Bunny Stream Library ID, Stream API Key, and CDN Pull Zone (all found in your Bunny dashboard under Stream → your library → API).
  4. Click Test Connection to confirm your credentials work.
  5. Click Sync Now to pull your existing videos into WordPress.
  6. Tag and categorize videos from Nahnu Video → All Videos using Quick Edit, same as you would with Posts.
  7. Insert videos with the [bunny_video] / [bunny_grid] / [bunny_playlist] shortcodes, or the “Nahnu Video” / “Nahnu Video Grid” / “Nahnu Video Playlist” blocks.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin upload or transcode video?

No. Video hosting, transcoding, and delivery are all handled by Bunny Stream directly. This plugin only connects your WordPress site to a library you already manage in Bunny’s dashboard.

Can I embed a video before syncing my whole library?

Yes. [bunny_video id="your-bunny-guid"] works with a raw Bunny video GUID directly, even before that video has been synced into WordPress.

I changed something in Bunny (title, cover photo, replaced the file) but WordPress still shows the old version. What do I do?

Click Sync Now again (Nahnu Video → Settings → Library Sync). Syncing doesn’t just pull in new videos, it also refreshes everything about videos you’ve already synced: title, duration, view count, and the cover photo/thumbnail. Turning on Auto-sync does this for you automatically on a schedule instead, and the optional Bunny webhook (Settings → Bunny Webhook) does it within seconds of the change. Either way, syncing never touches anything you’ve set yourself in WordPress, like categories, tags, or a video’s published/draft status.

What happens to a video I delete in Bunny?

The next full sync moves its WordPress post to the Trash, so it stops showing up on your site. It’s never deleted outright, so you can restore it from the Trash if that was a mistake. Developers can turn this off with the nahnu_video_remove_missing_on_sync filter.

Do I need to set up the Bunny webhook?

No, it’s optional. Without it, scheduled sync (or Sync Now) still picks everything up. With it, Bunny tells WordPress about new uploads, finished encodes and changes right away. Copy the URL from Nahnu Video → Settings → Bunny Webhook and paste it into Bunny under Stream → your library → API → Webhook URL. The URL contains a secret key, so treat it like a password; you can create a new one at any time.

Does deleting the plugin delete my videos?

Not from Bunny. Your Bunny Stream library is never modified by this plugin, in either direction. By default, deleting the plugin also leaves your synced WordPress data (videos, categories, tags, settings) untouched. There’s an opt-in “delete all data on uninstall” toggle under Settings → Advanced if you want a clean removal.

Is this an official Bunny.net plugin?

No. Nahnu Video is an independent, third-party integration built by Nahnu Plugins. It is not made by, affiliated with, or endorsed by Bunny.net.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • New: developer integration API for plugins that upload videos to Bunny Stream. Import, refresh, or remove one video by its GUID with nahnu_video_import(), nahnu_video_refresh(), nahnu_video_remove() or the matching actions, plus look-up functions by GUID, post ID, or Media Library attachment. See “For Developers”.
  • New: while Bunny is still encoding a newly imported video, Nahnu Video checks back automatically until the thumbnail and duration are final.
  • New: optional Bunny webhook (Settings → Bunny Webhook), so uploads, finished encodes and changes show up within seconds.
  • New: hooks and filters nahnu_video_bunny_credentials, nahnu_video_should_import, nahnu_video_insert_post_args, nahnu_video_remove_missing_on_sync, nahnu_video_refresh_retry_delays, nahnu_video_webhook_imports_new, nahnu_video_removed, nahnu_video_deleted, nahnu_video_webhook_received and nahnu_video_loaded.
  • New: nahnu_video_render() also accepts a post ID or Bunny GUID as its first argument.
  • Changed: Sync Now moves videos that were deleted in Bunny to the Trash (restorable), and its result shows how many.

1.0.0

  • Initial public release.
  • Bunny Stream library sync (manual or scheduled), with real WordPress categories and tags for organizing videos.
  • [bunny_video], [bunny_grid], and [bunny_playlist] shortcodes, plus matching “Nahnu Video”, “Nahnu Video Grid”, and “Nahnu Video Playlist” blocks with a searchable video picker and live preview.
  • Video Control admin screen: thumbnails, live search and instant category/tag filtering, one-click shortcode copy, and inline category/tag editing.
  • Shortcode Generator: pick videos, set every option, live preview, copy the exact shortcode.
  • Optional hover-preview thumbnails (off by default) using Bunny’s own preview clips.
  • Optional CDN Token Authentication support for Pull Zones with restricted direct file access.
  • Play count and watch-time statistics, with a PHP function and REST API for other plugins/themes to read them.
  • Settings page covering connection, playback defaults, label colors, default grid layout, and library sync.

short_description: Embed and organize Bunny Stream videos in WordPress with shortcodes and a block editor picker. A free Nahnu Plugins add-on for WP SuperDocs.

  • nahnu_video_insert_post_args( $post_args, $bunny_video, $is_new, $args ): change the post data before it’s saved, e.g. use the Media Library attachment’s title instead of Bunny’s file name.
  • nahnu_video_remove_missing_on_sync( $enabled ): return false to keep videos that no longer exist in Bunny.
  • nahnu_video_refresh_retry_delays( $delays, $guid ): seconds between “still encoding?” checks. An empty array turns them off.
  • nahnu_video_webhook_imports_new( $import, $guid ): return false so the webhook only refreshes existing videos.
  • nahnu_video_html( $html, $video, $atts ): change the final embed HTML for a video.
  • Also: nahnu_video_render_args, nahnu_video_grid_render_args, nahnu_video_grid_html, nahnu_video_embed_params, nahnu_video_cdn_urls, nahnu_video_query_args, nahnu_video_stats, nahnu_video_can_edit_terms, nahnu_video_default_settings.

REST endpoints

  • GET /wp-json/nahnu-video/v1/stats/{id} and GET /wp-json/nahnu-video/v1/stats: public, read-only play count and watch time.
  • POST /wp-json/nahnu-video/v1/bunny-webhook?key=...: receives Bunny Stream webhooks. Requires the secret key from Settings. The payload is only used to learn which video changed; that video’s data is always re-fetched from Bunny.

Other functions

nahnu_video_render_grid(), `nahnu_video_get_video_data()`, `nahnu_video_query()`, `nahnu_video_get_related()`, `nahnu_video_get_stats()`, `nahnu_video_get_top_videos()`, `nahnu_video_refresh_stats()`.<h3>Known Limitations</h3>

* If Hover Preview is turned on, thumbnails may not load in the block editor’s live preview for the Nahnu Video / Nahnu Video Grid blocks.
* The Nahnu Video Playlist block’s thumbnail grid may not load thumbnails in the block editor’s live preview.

Both of these are editor-preview issues only, what visitors actually see on the published page is unaffected. This is a free plugin maintained in our spare time, and this particular editor-preview quirk needs more time to track down properly than we’ve been able to give it so far. It’s also our first time building real block editor integration ourselves, we normally just build with shortcodes, so there’s a real learning curve on our end with how the block editor’s preview machinery works internally. We’re not too worried about it precisely because the front end works correctly; we’ll keep chipping away at the editor preview itself in a future update.
